title: Algebraize a map to a scalar extension, with torsion kernel and cokernel
statement: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings and $R\to S$ a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $I\subseteq R$ be a finitely generated ideal such that the induced map $R/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism. Call an $R$-module $I$-power torsion when for every element $x$ there is an integer $n\geq0$ such that $r x=0$ for every $r\in I^n$; for an $S$-module use restriction of scalars. Let $P$ be an $R$-module and $Q$ an $S$-module; write $S\otimes_R P$ for scalar extension and $\psi_S$ for scalar extension of a linear map [def-weil-module-base-change]. For an $S$-linear map $\varphi:Q\to S\otimes_R P$ with $I$-power torsion kernel and cokernel, there exist an $R$-module $T$, an $R$-linear map $\psi:T\to P$, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $\beta:Q\to S\otimes_R T$ such that $\psi_S\circ\beta=\varphi$, and both $\ker\psi$ and $P/\operatorname{im}\psi$ are $I$-power torsion.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (lemma-application-formal-glueing), proof of part (1), using Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data) and Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence); torsion follows by exact localization and finite generation as in step 5 of lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny

proof.text: Choose a finite generating family f for I, including the empty family when I=0. Apply the finite localization criterion to the restriction of the given S-linear map, obtaining bijectivity on each chart. Transport through the canonical prime-component identification and localize the inverse of that identification. Thus the map from Q to the canonical prime component is locally bijective.

Apply replacement of the prime component to the canonical datum of P. Obtain X with prime equivalent to Q and a morphism a to Can(P) whose charts are bijective. By essential surjectivity, choose T and an isomorphism Can(T) to X. By fullness lift its composite with a to an R-linear map psi:T to P.

Project the isomorphism to prime components, invert it and compose with the prime identification of Can(T), obtaining beta:Q to S tensor T. The prime component identity for Can.map psi implies psi_S composed with beta equals the original map. Projecting the same isomorphism to chart components shows each localized psi is bijective. Component transports use the prescribed object equalities and heterogeneous map equalities in the canonical-equivalence statement. Apply the finite localization criterion again to get ideal-power torsion kernel and cokernel of psi.
